args.body:
ACCOUNT CONTROL AGREEMENT
TRACKED-CHANGES REDLINE
(Counterparty Draft — Firm Response Markup)

Document: Account Control Agreement (Deposit Account)
Parties: [Secured Party / Administrative Agent] ("Secured Party"); [Debtor / Borrower] ("Debtor"); [Depository Bank] ("Bank")
Related Facility: Senior Secured Credit Agreement dated as of [Closing Date] (as amended, the "Credit Agreement")
Accounts: See Schedule I (Account Details)
Governing Form Baseline: Bank standard form ACA, as modified to conform to Credit Agreement §9.01 / Collateral Package and Firm ACA Playbook v4.2
Redline Legend: [DELETE: text to be deleted]  [INSERT: text to be inserted]  [MOVE / COMMENT] as noted
Status: Counsel markup for circulation to counterparty; incorporates playbook, Credit Agreement, Bank form, Schedule/Exhibit reconciliation, and controlling deal-team instruction dated [latest partner email]

================================================================================
PREAMBLE / RECITALS
================================================================================

This ACCOUNT CONTROL AGREEMENT (this "Agreement") is entered into as of [Effective Date], by and among Debtor, Secured Party, and Bank.

Recitals.

A. Debtor has granted Secured Party a security interest in the Deposit Accounts described on Schedule I (each, an "Account" and collectively, the "Accounts") pursuant to the Credit Agreement and the other Collateral Documents.

B. The parties are entering into this Agreement to perfect Secured Party's security interest in the Accounts by "control" under Article 9 of the Uniform Commercial Code as in effect in the State of New York (the "UCC"), and to establish the relative rights and duties of the parties with respect to the Accounts.

C. [INSERT: Bank's standard form terms apply only to the extent not inconsistent with this Agreement, the Credit Agreement, and the irrevocable instructions set forth herein. In the event of conflict among this Agreement, Bank's deposit account terms, and the Credit Agreement regarding control, entitlement orders, or priority of Secured Party's interest, this Agreement and the Credit Agreement shall control as between Debtor and Secured Party, and Bank shall honor the control and entitlement-order mechanics of this Agreement.]

================================================================================
ARTICLE I — DEFINITIONS
================================================================================

Section 1.1  Definitions. Capitalized terms used but not defined herein have the meanings assigned in the Credit Agreement. As used herein:

"Account" / "Accounts" — as defined in the Recitals and listed on Schedule I, including all sub-accounts, replacements, renumberings, and proceeds.

"Business Day" — [INSERT: as defined in the Credit Agreement; if Bank's definition is narrower, the Credit Agreement definition controls for notice and entitlement-order timing as between Debtor and Secured Party, provided Bank receives notice in accordance with Section 6.1.]

"Entitlement Order" — an order directing disposition of funds in an Account, given by Secured Party to Bank in accordance with this Agreement (including a Notice of Exclusive Control).

"Indemnified Person" — [INSERT: Secured Party, Bank (solely in its capacity as depository under this Agreement and subject to Section 5.2), and each of their respective officers, directors, employees, agents, and Related Parties, in each case to the extent indemnified under Article V.]

"Material Adverse Effect" — [DELETE: any material adverse effect on the business, assets, or financial condition of Debtor, other than any effect arising from or relating to (i) changes in law or regulation, (ii) any regulatory inquiry, investigation, action, or proceeding by a Governmental Authority, (iii) market or industry conditions, or (iv) the announcement or pendency of the transactions contemplated by the Credit Agreement.]
[INSERT: "Material Adverse Effect" has the meaning assigned to such term in the Credit Agreement; provided that, for purposes of this Agreement only, no MAE determination shall be required as a condition to Secured Party's right to deliver a Notice of Exclusive Control or Entitlement Order. Without limiting the Credit Agreement definition, and notwithstanding any disclosure on Schedule 3.7 of the Credit Agreement or any analogous schedule, effects arising from regulatory inquiries, investigations, actions, or proceedings (including the two pending regulatory inquiries disclosed on Schedule 3.7) shall NOT be carved out of MAE solely by reason of such disclosure when assessing Debtor's covenants, default-related triggers, or indemnity obligations under this Agreement. Schedule 3.7 disclosures qualify representations under the Credit Agreement as expressly provided therein but do not (a) dilute perfection or control, (b) condition Entitlement Orders, or (c) expand MAE carve-outs under this Agreement.]

[COMMENT — MAE: Counterparty added regulatory-action carve-outs that directly intersect Schedule 3.7 pending inquiries. Playbook and Credit Agreement alignment require rejection of those carve-outs in the ACA. See Issues/Risk Memo Issue 2.]

"Notice of Exclusive Control" or "NEC" — written notice from Secured Party to Bank that Secured Party is exercising exclusive control over the Accounts.

"Obligations" — [INSERT: all Obligations under and as defined in the Credit Agreement and the other Loan Documents, including contingent and swap/cash-management obligations secured by the Collateral Documents.]

"UCC" — as defined in the Recitals; references to control mean control under UCC §§9-104 and, as applicable, 8-106 / 9-106.

Section 1.2  Rules of Construction. [INSERT: Headings are for convenience only. The words "include," "includes," and "including" are deemed to be followed by "without limitation." References to Schedules and Exhibits are to those attached hereto, which are incorporated by reference. Scheduled exceptions in Credit Agreement disclosure schedules control the scope of Credit Agreement representations as stated therein, but do not amend this Agreement unless expressly cross-incorporated by section reference herein.]

================================================================================
ARTICLE II — ESTABLISHMENT OF CONTROL; ACCOUNT DETAILS
================================================================================

Section 2.1  Account Identification.
(a) Bank confirms that Debtor is the Bank's customer with respect to each Account listed on Schedule I.
(b) [INSERT: Schedule I shall set forth, for each Account: bank name and ABA/routing number; account name; account number; account type (operating, concentration, reserve, proceeds, etc.); currency; branch location; and whether the Account is a "Blocked Account," "Collection Account," or other designated collateral account under the Credit Agreement.]
(c) [INSERT: Debtor and Bank shall not change account numbers, titles, or location of any Account, or close any Account, without prior written consent of Secured Party, except that Bank may implement commercially reasonable renumbering upon not less than ten (10) Business Days' prior written notice to Secured Party and Debtor, with automatic amendment of Schedule I.]

Section 2.2  Control.
(a) Bank agrees that it will comply with Entitlement Orders originated by Secured Party directing disposition of funds in the Accounts without further consent by Debtor.
(b) [INSERT: Bank subordinates any security interest, lien, right of setoff, or recoupment Bank may have in the Accounts to the security interest of Secured Party, except for (i) Bank's fees and charges for maintaining the Accounts, (ii) returned items, and (iii) overdrafts advanced by Bank in the ordinary course, in each case not to exceed the amounts and subject to the notice mechanics in Section 5.3 (Bank's Limited Recourse).]
(c) [DELETE: Debtor may freely withdraw and direct disposition of funds until Bank receives a Notice of Exclusive Control AND five (5) Business Days have elapsed.]
[INSERT: Until Bank receives a Notice of Exclusive Control, Debtor may operate the Accounts and direct disposition of funds in the ordinary course, subject to the Credit Agreement cash-management and blocked-account covenants. Upon Bank's receipt of a Notice of Exclusive Control, Bank shall immediately cease complying with Debtor instructions and shall comply solely with Secured Party Entitlement Orders. No cure period, waiting period, or Debtor consent shall condition Bank's obligation to honor an NEC or Entitlement Order. (Alignment to Bank standard form control mechanics and Credit Agreement §[Blocked Accounts].)]

Section 2.3  Notice of Exclusive Control; Entitlement Orders.
(a) Secured Party may deliver an NEC and/or Entitlement Orders at any time in its sole discretion exercised in accordance with the Loan Documents.
(b) [INSERT: Bank shall confirm receipt of any NEC or Entitlement Order by email or other electronic means to the contacts on Schedule II within one (1) Business Day.]
(c) [INSERT: Bank is not required to investigate authenticity beyond the notice mechanics in Article VI, and may rely on notices appearing on their face to be from Secured Party.]

Section 2.4  No Other Control Agreements. [INSERT: Debtor represents it has not entered, and covenants it will not enter, into any other control agreement or similar arrangement with respect to the Accounts without Secured Party's prior written consent.]

================================================================================
ARTICLE III — REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES
================================================================================

Section 3.1  Debtor Representations. Debtor represents and warrants to Secured Party and Bank that:
(a) organization, power, and authority to execute and perform this Agreement;
(b) this Agreement constitutes a legal, valid, and binding obligation enforceable against Debtor;
(c) the Accounts are genuine and in existence, Debtor is the sole customer, and the account details on Schedule I are true and complete;
(d) [INSERT: except for the security interest in favor of Secured Party and permitted Bank liens under Section 2.2(b), Debtor has not granted any other security interest or control right in the Accounts;]
(e) [INSERT: execution and performance do not conflict with law, organizational documents, or material agreements, and do not require consents that have not been obtained;]
(f) [DELETE: there is no pending or, to Debtor's knowledge, threatened regulatory inquiry, investigation, or proceeding that could reasonably be expected to affect the Accounts or Debtor's authority, other than matters that would not have a Material Adverse Effect (as modified by regulatory carve-outs).]
[INSERT: except as expressly set forth on Schedule 3.7 to the Credit Agreement (which discloses two pending regulatory inquiries), there is no pending or, to Debtor's knowledge, threatened legal or regulatory proceeding that challenges Secured Party's security interest, Bank's ability to comply with Entitlement Orders, or Debtor's authority to grant control. Schedule 3.7 does not qualify or limit Sections 2.2, 2.3, 4.1, or Article V of this Agreement.]

Section 3.2  Bank Representations. Bank represents that:
(a) it is a [bank / branch] maintaining the Accounts in the ordinary course;
(b) the account records identify Debtor as customer;
(c) [INSERT: Bank has not entered into any currently effective agreement with any third party to comply with instructions concerning the Accounts subordinate to or on parity with Secured Party's rights hereunder (other than standard clearing/settlement arrangements);]
(d) [INSERT: this Agreement is effective to establish control in favor of Secured Party under UCC §9-104.]

Section 3.3  Survival of Representations.
[DELETE: The representations and warranties in this Agreement shall survive execution for a period of twelve (12) months following the Effective Date, after which no claim may be made in respect thereof.]
[INSERT: The representations and warranties in this Agreement shall survive the execution and delivery of this Agreement, the establishment of control, any NEC, and any termination of this Agreement solely as to matters arising prior to termination, and shall survive co-extensively with the survival periods set forth in Exhibit B (Survival Matrix) attached hereto and in the Credit Agreement indemnification and survival provisions. Without limiting the foregoing: (i) representations as to organization, authority, enforceability, creation and perfection/control of security interests, and Brokers/Bank status shall survive indefinitely (or until expiration of the applicable statute of limitations); (ii) other fundamental representations shall survive for not less than the longest survival period applicable to corresponding representations under the Credit Agreement; and (iii) no amendment to survival in this Agreement shall be effective unless it conforms to Exhibit B. Any counterparty proposal to shorten survival below Exhibit B is rejected.]

[COMMENT — SURVIVAL: Walk-away issue per controlling deal-team correspondence. Exhibit B controls. Counterparty's 12-month limitation period is deleted in full. See Issues/Risk Memo Issue 3.]

================================================================================
ARTICLE IV — COVENANTS; OPERATION OF ACCOUNTS
================================================================================

Section 4.1  Debtor Covenants. Debtor covenants that it shall:
(a) maintain the Accounts solely at Bank and as identified on Schedule I;
(b) [INSERT: direct all proceeds of Collateral required by the Credit Agreement into the appropriate Accounts;]
(c) not permit any other person to have control over the Accounts;
(d) [INSERT: provide Secured Party and Bank prompt notice of any attachment, levy, regulatory freeze, or competing claim affecting any Account, including any development in the Schedule 3.7 inquiries that could affect the Accounts or Bank's performance;]
(e) execute further assurances reasonably requested to maintain control and perfection.

Section 4.2  Bank Covenants. Bank shall:
(a) maintain the Accounts as deposit accounts under the UCC;
(b) not agree to comply with instructions from any person other than Debtor (prior to NEC) or Secured Party (from and after NEC / as to Entitlement Orders) concerning the Accounts, except as required by law or clearing rules;
(c) [INSERT: provide monthly account statements to Secured Party concurrently with Debtor, and provide online view access to Secured Party if available;]
(d) [INSERT: notify Secured Party promptly upon Bank's becoming aware of any competing control agreement, levy, or freeze.]

Section 4.3  Cash Management Alignment. [INSERT: Operation of the Accounts shall be consistent with Credit Agreement cash-management, blocked-account, and dominion provisions. This Agreement is a Loan Document.]

================================================================================
ARTICLE V — INDEMNIFICATION; LIMITATION OF LIABILITY; BANK PROTECTIONS
================================================================================

Section 5.1  Debtor Indemnity.
(a) Debtor shall indemnify, defend, and hold harmless each Indemnified Person from and against any and all claims, damages, losses, liabilities, costs, and expenses (including reasonable and documented out-of-pocket attorneys' fees) arising out of or relating to this Agreement, the Accounts, Bank's compliance with Entitlement Orders, or any Debtor instruction, except to the extent resulting from the Indemnified Person's gross negligence or willful misconduct as determined by a final non-appealable judgment.
(b) Indemnification Cap.
[DELETE: Debtor's aggregate liability under this Article V shall not exceed $[X/2] (the "Indemnification Cap").]
[INSERT: Debtor's aggregate liability under this Article V for monetary damages (other than Excluded Matters) shall not exceed the Indemnification Cap equal to $[X] [RESTORE FIRM/PLAYBOOK CAP — full playbook cap amount; silently reduced counterparty figure is rejected], provided that the Indemnification Cap shall NOT apply to: (i) Debtor's fraud or willful misconduct; (ii) failure to pay Bank's ordinary account fees when due; (iii) Debtor's breach of Sections 2.1, 2.2, 2.4, 3.1(c)-(d), or 4.1 (control, title, and no-competing-control covenants); (iv) third-party claims arising from Debtor's misdirection of funds or unauthorized grants of control; or (v) retained liabilities described on Schedule 5.2 to the Credit Agreement to the extent Debtor attempts to shift such liabilities to Secured Party or Bank through this Agreement (collectively, "Excluded Matters"). Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities remain Debtor's responsibility and are not reduced, capped, or re-allocated by this Article V.]

(c) Basket / Deductible.
[DELETE: No indemnification claim may be made unless and until claims in the aggregate exceed $[Basket], after which Debtor shall be liable for all claims from dollar one (tipping basket).]
[INSERT — PER CONTROLLING CLIENT INSTRUCTION CONCEDING BASKET CONVERSION: No indemnification claim (other than for Excluded Matters) may be made unless and until the aggregate amount of otherwise indemnifiable claims exceeds $[Basket] (the "Basket"), after which Debtor shall be liable for all such claims from dollar one (tipping basket). Excluded Matters are not subject to the Basket. For the avoidance of doubt, the parties acknowledge the Basket is a tipping basket (not a deductible), as conceded by Secured Party solely with respect to basket mechanics and without prejudice to the Indemnification Cap restoration and Excluded Matters above.]

[COMMENT — INDEMNITY CAP: Silent reduction rejected; restore playbook/Credit Agreement-aligned cap. BASKET: Client concedes conversion from deductible to tipping basket per latest partner instruction. SCHEDULE 5.2: Retained liabilities must not be shifted by cap/basket mechanics. See Issues/Risk Memo Issues 1 and 4.]

Section 5.2  Bank Standard of Care; Reliance.
(a) Bank shall not be liable for any action taken or omitted in good faith in accordance with this Agreement or Entitlement Orders, except for Bank's gross negligence or willful misconduct.
(b) [INSERT: Bank may rely on any notice, NEC, or Entitlement Order believed in good faith to be genuine and authorized.]
(c) [INSERT: In no event shall Bank be liable for consequential, special, or punitive damages.]

Section 5.3  Bank's Limited Recourse / Fees / Setoff.
[INSERT: Bank may charge the Accounts for its customary fees and for returned items and ordinary-course overdrafts. Bank shall provide Secured Party concurrent notice of any setoff or freeze exercised against an Account. Bank's aggregate priority for fees, returned items, and overdrafts shall not exceed the amounts customary under Bank's standard form as attached as Exhibit C, and shall not impair Secured Party's control.]

Section 5.4  Secured Party Liability. [INSERT: Secured Party shall have no liability to Bank or Debtor for actions taken pursuant to the Loan Documents in good faith. Secured Party's obligations hereunder are solely administrative as agent to the extent applicable under the Credit Agreement.]

================================================================================
ARTICLE VI — NOTICES
================================================================================

Section 6.1  Notices. All notices, NECs, and Entitlement Orders shall be in writing and delivered by hand, nationally recognized overnight courier, or email (with confirmation of transmission) to the addresses set forth on Schedule II.
[INSERT: Email notice is effective upon transmission if sent on a Business Day before 5:00 p.m. recipient local time (or next Business Day). NEC and Entitlement Orders delivered by email to Bank's designated operations contact on Schedule II are effective upon receipt.]

================================================================================
ARTICLE VII — TERMINATION; AMENDMENTS
================================================================================

Section 7.1  Termination.
(a) This Agreement shall terminate upon the first to occur of: (i) written notice from Secured Party to Bank that all Obligations have been paid in full and commitments terminated, and Secured Party releases control; (ii) written agreement of all parties; or (iii) [INSERT: transfer of the Accounts with Secured Party's prior written consent and execution of a replacement control agreement in form and substance satisfactory to Secured Party].
(b) [INSERT: Termination shall not affect rights or obligations accrued prior to termination, including indemnity and survival under Section 3.3 and Article V.]

Section 7.2  Amendments. [INSERT: No amendment or waiver is effective unless in writing and signed by Debtor, Secured Party, and Bank (except that Secured Party and Debtor may amend provisions that do not increase Bank's duties or liabilities without Bank's signature). Silence or course of performance is not a waiver.]

================================================================================
ARTICLE VIII — MISCELLANEOUS
================================================================================

Section 8.1  Governing Law. This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of New York (without regard to conflicts principles), including the UCC as in effect in New York. [INSERT: Control is determined under New York UCC §9-304 / §9-104 as applicable.]

Section 8.2  Jurisdiction; Waiver of Jury Trial. [INSERT: Exclusive jurisdiction in the state or federal courts located in the Borough of Manhattan, New York City. EACH PARTY WAIVES JURY TRIAL TO THE MAXIMUM EXTENT PERMITTED BY LAW.]

Section 8.3  Severability; Counterparts; Electronic Signatures. [Standard firm language INSERT if absent from counterparty draft.]

Section 8.4  Entire Agreement; Conflict. [INSERT: This Agreement, together with the Credit Agreement and Collateral Documents as among Debtor and Secured Party, constitutes the entire agreement as to control of the Accounts. If any conflict exists between this Agreement and Bank's depositary terms regarding control or Entitlement Orders, this Agreement controls. If any conflict exists between this Agreement and the Credit Agreement regarding Debtor's obligations to Secured Party, the Credit Agreement controls as between Debtor and Secured Party, provided Bank may rely on this Agreement.]

Section 8.5  UCC Priority; No Petition. [INSERT: Bank agrees not to contest Secured Party's perfected security interest by control. Debtor agrees this Agreement is a Loan Document and breaches hereof are Defaults/Events of Default as provided in the Credit Agreement.]

Section 8.6  Further Assurances. [INSERT.]

================================================================================
SCHEDULE I — ACCOUNT DETAILS
================================================================================

[INSERT complete account block for each Account:]

Account 1:
- Bank / Branch:
- ABA / Routing No.:
- Account Name:
- Account Number:
- Account Type: [Operating / Concentration / Proceeds / Reserve]
- Currency: USD
- Designation under Credit Agreement: [Blocked Account / Collection Account / etc.]
- Existing control agreements: None (or list and subordinate/terminate)

Account 2: [same fields]

[INSERT: Any omission of an Account required under the Credit Agreement collateral package is not a waiver; Debtor and Bank shall amend Schedule I within five (5) Business Days of Secured Party notice.]

================================================================================
SCHEDULE II — NOTICE ADDRESSES
================================================================================

Debtor: [ ]
Secured Party / Administrative Agent: [ ]
Bank (relationship and operations/entitlement-order desk): [ ]
With copies as required by Credit Agreement.

================================================================================
EXHIBIT A — FORM OF NOTICE OF EXCLUSIVE CONTROL
================================================================================

[INSERT Bank-acceptable form NEC referencing this Agreement and Schedule I Accounts; effective on receipt; no Debtor consent or cure period.]

================================================================================
EXHIBIT B — SURVIVAL MATRIX
================================================================================

[RETAIN AND GIVE CONTROLLING EFFECT — DO NOT SHORTEN]

Category                                          | Survival Period
--------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------
Organization, authority, enforceability           | Indefinite / statute of limitations
Creation, perfection, and priority of control     | Indefinite / statute of limitations
Account title, exclusivity of customer status     | Indefinite / statute of limitations
No competing control / no other liens (as given)  | Co-extensive with Credit Agreement fundamental reps; not less than SOL
Other Debtor representations                      | Per Credit Agreement survival for analogous reps; floor = Exhibit B
Indemnity claims for Excluded Matters             | SOL
Other indemnity claims                            | As provided in Article V and Credit Agreement

[DELETE any counterparty limitation period that shortens the above, including any flat 12-month survival for "core representations."]

================================================================================
EXHIBIT C — BANK STANDARD FORM FEE AND SETOFF PARAMETERS
================================================================================

[INSERT conforming extract from Bank standard form: fee schedule reference; returned item and overdraft priority caps; statement that control mechanics of this Agreement supersede inconsistent Bank boilerplate.]

================================================================================
SIGNATURE BLOCKS
================================================================================

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the parties have executed this Agreement as of the date first written above.

DEBTOR:                    [signature block]
SECURED PARTY:             [signature block]
BANK:                      [signature block]

================================================================================
END OF REDLINE

args.body:
ISSUES AND RISK MEMORANDUM
Account Control Agreement — Counterparty Paper Review

TO:      Deal Team / File
FROM:    Contracts Counsel
RE:      Review of Counterparty Draft Account Control Agreement — Deviations, Missing Protections, Off-Market Terms, and Recommended Positions
MATTER:  contracts work: Review Account Control Agreement Counterparty Paper
RELATED: Credit Agreement (executed); Firm ACA Playbook v4.2; Depository Bank standard form ACA; Schedule I account details; Schedules 3.7 and 5.2; Exhibit B Survival Matrix; Deal correspondence (controlling partner instruction)
OUTPUTS: aca-redline.docx (tracked-changes response markup); this issues-risk-memo.docx

================================================================================
I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
================================================================================

We reviewed the counterparty's draft Account Control Agreement ("ACA") against (i) the firm internal ACA playbook, (ii) the executed Credit Agreement and collateral package, (iii) the depository bank's standard form, (iv) account-detail and notice checklists, and (v) disclosure schedules/exhibits and controlling deal-team correspondence.

The counterparty draft accepts most firm-standard control architecture but introduces three primary negotiated deviations, each of which intersects disclosure-schedule qualifications:

  (1) Silent reduction of the indemnification cap, and conversion of the indemnity basket from a deductible to a tipping basket;
  (2) Expansion of the Material Adverse Effect definition with regulatory-action carve-outs that overlap Schedule 3.7 pending inquiries; and
  (3) A new limitation period shortening survival for core representations, contradicting Exhibit B.

Controlling client instruction (latest partner email): concede the basket conversion (deductible → tipping basket); treat any survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue. Earlier contrary priority ordering in the thread is superseded.

Recommended posture reflected in aca-redline.docx:
  • RESTORE full indemnification cap; REJECT silent reduction; add Excluded Matters so Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities cannot be shifted.
  • CONCEDE tipping basket (per controlling instruction), expressly and narrowly.
  • REJECT MAE regulatory carve-outs; neutralize Schedule 3.7 spillover into control/NEC/indemnity.
  • REJECT survival shortening; restore Exhibit B matrix (walk-away).
  • INSERT missing Bank-form and playbook control protections (immediate NEC; Bank lien subordination with customary exceptions; account detail fields; Loan Document status; conflict rules; further assurances).

Overall transaction risk if counterparty draft accepted without redline: HIGH as to perfection/control durability and indemnity economics; CRITICAL as to survival. With the attached redline, residual risk is LOW–MODERATE and consistent with market ACA practice for sponsored credit facilities.

================================================================================
II. CONTROLLING INSTRUCTIONS AND INTERPRETIVE RULES
================================================================================

1. Latest deal-team correspondence controls: client concedes basket conversion; survival-period reduction is walk-away. Superseded earlier messages stating the opposite priority are disregarded.
2. Disclosure schedules control over general base-document statements where they qualify representations: Schedule 3.7 (two pending regulatory inquiries); Schedule 5.2 (retained liabilities); Exhibit B (survival matrix).
3. Unrelated administrative correspondence misfiled in the matter folder is disregarded in full.
4. Bank standard form supplies market baseline for control mechanics, reliance, fee/setoff priority, and NEC effectiveness; Credit Agreement supplies baseline for Obligations, MAE, cash dominion, and Loan Document status; Playbook supplies non-negotiable lender-side protections and checklist items.

================================================================================
III. ISSUE-BY-ISSUE ANALYSIS
================================================================================

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 1 — Indemnification Cap Silently Reduced
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ACA Section(s):            Article V (Indemnification), §5.1(b)
Playbook Requirement:      Maintain full playbook/Credit Agreement-aligned aggregate indemnification cap; no silent reductions; carve out fundamental control breaches, fraud/willful misconduct, and third-party misdirection claims from any cap.
Credit Agreement / Schedules: Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities that must remain Debtor's economic responsibility; cap reduction would silently shift residual exposure toward Secured Party/Bank.
Bank Form:                 Bank expects robust Debtor indemnity for honoring Entitlement Orders; reduced cap increases Bank friction and may prompt Bank pushback or expanded Bank disclaimers.
Counterparty Deviation:    Cap reduced without callout (silent) to approximately half of playbook level (or otherwise below agreed economics).
Risk Rating:               HIGH
Exposure Analysis:         If a control failure, competing claim, or Entitlement Order dispute generates losses above the reduced cap, Secured Party and potentially Bank bear the uncovered delta. Interacts with Schedule 5.2: retained liabilities that Debtor already scheduled could be argued into the capped pool, effectively transferring scheduled Debtor liabilities to the secured side up to the gap between full and reduced cap. In a downside scenario involving regulatory freeze + competing claimant (see Issue 2 / Schedule 3.7), uncovered indemnity can become material relative to Account balances and enforcement costs.
Recommended Position:      REJECT silent cap reduction. RESTORE full cap. ADD express "Excluded Matters" outside the cap: fraud/willful misconduct; control/title/no-competing-control breaches; third-party claims from misdirection; and Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities. Implemented in aca-redline.docx §5.1(b).
Fallback:                  If commercial pressure requires a number between reduced and full cap, do not go below Credit Agreement indemnity economics; never allow Schedule 5.2 items inside the cap.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 2 — Material Adverse Effect: Regulatory-Action Carve-Outs
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ACA Section(s):            §1.1 (Definition of Material Adverse Effect); related use in §3.1 (Debtor representations) and any default/trigger cross-references
Playbook Requirement:      ACA should not re-litigate MAE. Prefer cross-reference to Credit Agreement MAE. ACA rights to NEC and Entitlement Orders must not be conditioned on MAE. No regulatory carve-outs that neutralize known deal risks.
Credit Agreement / Schedules: Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries. Those disclosures qualify Credit Agreement representations as provided in the schedules; they must NOT be bootstrapped into ACA MAE carve-outs that impair control, NEC rights, covenants, or indemnity.
Bank Form:                 Bank form does not condition control on MAE; injecting MAE carve-outs creates ambiguity Bank will not want to police.
Counterparty Deviation:    Adds carve-outs for regulatory action/inquiry/investigation/proceeding of the same type disclosed on Schedule 3.7, plus other standard seller-style MAE carve-outs inappropriate for an ACA.
Risk Rating:               HIGH
Exposure Analysis:         The carve-outs map onto the exact risk profile already disclosed. If a Schedule 3.7 inquiry escalates to a freeze, restraint, or authority challenge affecting the Accounts, Debtor could argue no MAE and attempt to blunt covenant/default or indemnity consequences under the ACA. Even if NEC remains technically available, MAE-linked representation bring-downs or termination rhetoric can delay enforcement and create litigation leverage. Off-market for ACAs, which are perfection/control instruments, not business MAE vehicles.
Recommended Position:      DELETE counterparty MAE definition. INSERT Credit Agreement MAE cross-reference; expressly state MAE is not a condition to NEC/Entitlement Orders; expressly state Schedule 3.7 does not dilute §§2.2, 2.3, 4.1, or Article V. Tighten §3.1 regulatory rep to preserve Schedule 3.7 disclosure for Credit Agreement purposes only. Implemented in aca-redline.docx §§1.1, 3.1(f), 4.1(d).
Fallback:                  None recommended on regulatory carve-out; limited market MAE carve-outs unrelated to known inquiries may be discussed only if MAE remains irrelevant to NEC.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 3 — Survival / Limitation Period Shortened for Core Representations
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ACA Section(s):            §3.3 (Survival of Representations); interaction with Exhibit B Survival Matrix; Article V claims timing
Playbook Requirement:      Fundamental reps (authority, enforceability, control/perfection, account title, no competing control) survive indefinitely or for the applicable statute of limitations; other reps track Credit Agreement survival floors; Exhibit B is controlling.
Credit Agreement / Schedules: Exhibit B sets the survival matrix. Counterparty's limitation period contradicts Exhibit B and would undercut post-closing claims for core control reps.
Bank Form:                 Bank relies on continuing accuracy of account status and authority reps when honoring Entitlement Orders over the life of the facility.
Counterparty Deviation:    New limitation period shortens survival for core representations (counterparty proposal effectively ~12 months from Effective Date, after which no claim may be made).
Risk Rating:               CRITICAL (WALK-AWAY)
Exposure Analysis:         Control defects, competing control agreements, and account-title problems often surface only upon enforcement, refinance, or insolvency—frequently well after 12 months. A short survival window extinguishes practical remedies precisely when needed, and may be argued to narrow indemnity for representation-based claims. Direct conflict with Exhibit B. Controlling client instruction: any survival-period reduction is a walk-away issue.
Recommended Position:      REJECT in full. DELETE short limitation period. INSERT survival co-extensive with Exhibit B and Credit Agreement; indefinite/SOL survival for fundamental control and authority reps; no amendment of survival unless conforming to Exhibit B. Implemented in aca-redline.docx §3.3 and Exhibit B.
Fallback:                  None. Per controlling instruction, do not trade survival for other concessions.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 4 — Indemnity Basket Converted from Deductible to Tipping Basket
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ACA Section(s):            §5.1(c)
Playbook Requirement:      Prefer deductible basket (Debtor bears claims only above basket; first-dollar below basket stays with claimant) for ACA indemnity hygiene; tipping basket is more Debtor-friendly once threshold is crossed.
Credit Agreement / Schedules: Economics should not allow basket mechanics to absorb or re-characterize Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities.
Bank Form:                 Neutral to basket type if Bank is fully indemnified for following orders; Bank cares more about uncapped/excluded fundamental items.
Counterparty Deviation:    Converts basket from deductible to tipping basket (once aggregate claims exceed basket, liability relates back to dollar one).
Risk Rating:               MODERATE (CONCEDE per client instruction)
Exposure Analysis:         Relative to a deductible, a tipping basket increases Debtor's liability once the threshold is exceeded (first-dollar after tip). Net effect is not uniformly "pro-Debtor": deductible protects Debtor on small claims below the basket; tipping basket hurts Debtor after tip but can encourage claim aggregation. Client has instructed concession of this conversion. Residual risk is acceptable if (i) cap is restored (Issue 1), (ii) Excluded Matters sit outside basket and cap, and (iii) Schedule 5.2 items remain Excluded Matters.
Recommended Position:      CONCEDE tipping basket expressly, narrowly, and without prejudice to cap restoration and Excluded Matters. Implemented in aca-redline.docx §5.1(c).
Fallback:                  N/A — conceded.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 5 — Missing / Weak Control Mechanics vs. Bank Standard Form and UCC Practice
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ACA Section(s):            §§2.2–2.3 (Control; NEC; Entitlement Orders); §2.1 (Account identification); §5.2–5.3 (Bank reliance, fees, setoff)
Playbook Requirement:      Immediate effectiveness of NEC upon Bank receipt; no Debtor cure period; Bank agrees to comply with Secured Party Entitlement Orders without Debtor consent; Bank subordinates liens/setoff subject to customary fee/returned-item/overdraft exceptions; account schedule completeness; dual statements/access.
Credit Agreement:          Blocked-account / cash dominion regime assumes effective control at enforcement.
Bank Form:                 Standard form provides immediate NEC, reliance, limited Bank liability, and customary priority for fees/returned items/overdrafts.
Counterparty Deviation:    Draft included a post-NEC waiting/cure concept (multi-Business Day lag before exclusive control) and thin treatment of Bank subordination, account detail fields, and reliance.
Risk Rating:               HIGH (perfection/enforcement timing)
Exposure Analysis:         Any post-NEC lag is off-market and creates a window for Debtor drains, preferential transfers, or competing process. Incomplete Schedule I fields impair practical control and audit. Absence of clear Bank lien subordination invites priority fights at enforcement.
Recommended Position:      DELETE waiting/cure period. INSERT immediate NEC; Bank subordination with customary exceptions; Schedule I field requirements; Bank confirmation of receipt; reliance and fee parameters (Exhibit C). Implemented in aca-redline.docx Article II and §§5.2–5.3.
Fallback:                  Same-day operational acknowledgment only; no Debtor-facing cure.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 6 — Schedule 3.7 Intersection (Pending Regulatory Inquiries)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ACA Section(s):            §§1.1 (MAE), 3.1(f), 4.1(d)
Playbook / Schedule Rule:  Scheduled exceptions narrow Credit Agreement reps as stated; they do not amend ACA control rights unless expressly incorporated.
Counterparty Deviation:    MAE carve-outs and softened regulatory reps effectively export Schedule 3.7 into the ACA as a defense.
Risk Rating:               HIGH
Exposure Analysis:         Two pending inquiries are known. If either expands to payment-system, banking, or asset-freeze remedies, Secured Party needs unambiguous entitlement-order rights and notice covenants—not MAE debates.
Recommended Position:      Preserve Schedule 3.7 as Credit Agreement disclosure only; add prompt-notice covenant for developments affecting Accounts; block MAE/rep spillover. See redline §§1.1, 3.1(f), 4.1(d).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 7 — Schedule 5.2 Intersection (Retained Liabilities)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ACA Section(s):            §5.1 (Indemnity cap/basket)
Playbook / Schedule Rule:  Retained liabilities on Schedule 5.2 stay with Debtor; indemnity mechanics must not reallocate them to Secured Party/Bank.
Counterparty Deviation:    Cap reduction + basket redesign without Excluded Matters carve-out for Schedule 5.2 creates silent shift risk.
Risk Rating:               HIGH
Exposure Analysis:         At enforcement or claim settlement, Debtor may argue scheduled retained liabilities are ordinary indemnity claims subject to reduced cap/basket, leaving Secured Party with uncompensated collateral shortfalls.
Recommended Position:      Express Excluded Matters including Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities; restore cap. See redline §5.1(b)–(c).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 8 — Exhibit B Survival Matrix Contradiction
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ACA Section(s):            §3.3; Exhibit B
Deviation:                 Counterparty limitation period vs. Exhibit B matrix.
Risk Rating:               CRITICAL (WALK-AWAY)
Recommended Position:      Exhibit B controls; short survival deleted. See Issue 3.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 9 — Missing Playbook Checklist Items (Off-Market Omissions)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ACA Section(s):            Various (Preamble conflict rule; §2.4 no other control agreements; §4.3 Loan Document/cash-management alignment; §7.1 termination residual duties; §8 conflict, jury waiver, NY law/UCC control)
Playbook Requirement:      ACA is a Loan Document; conflict rule favoring control terms; no competing control agreements; further assurances; jury waiver; NY law; termination without prejudice to accrued indemnity/survival.
Counterparty Deviation:   Omissions / thin boilerplate relative to playbook and Bank form.
Risk Rating:               MODERATE (collectively HIGH if aggregated at enforcement)
Exposure Analysis:         Omissions rarely matter in clear performing scenarios; they become decisive in multi-creditor, insolvency, or Bank-operations disputes.
Recommended Position:      INSERT all checklist items as shown in aca-redline.docx Articles II, IV, VII, and VIII.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ISSUE 10 — Account Details and Operational Completeness
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ACA Section(s):            Schedule I; Schedule II; Exhibit A (form NEC)
Playbook / Bank Form:      Complete account identifiers; operations contact for Entitlement Orders; form NEC.
Counterparty Deviation:   Insufficient structured account fields and notice architecture in draft paper.
Risk Rating:               MODERATE
Recommended Position:      Populate Schedule I/II per checklist; attach form NEC as Exhibit A; automatic Schedule I update mechanics for Bank renumbering.

================================================================================
IV. SUMMARY DEVIATION MATRIX
================================================================================

ID | Topic                         | ACA §        | Source Conflict              | Direction vs. Playbook/CA/Bank | Risk       | Client Posture              | Redline Disposition
---|-------------------------------|--------------|------------------------------|--------------------------------|------------|-----------------------------|--------------------
1  | Indemnification cap reduction | §5.1(b)      | Playbook; Sch. 5.2           | Off-market silent cut          | HIGH       | Reject; restore             | Cap restored; Excluded Matters added
2  | MAE regulatory carve-outs     | §1.1, §3.1   | Playbook; CA MAE; Sch. 3.7   | Off-market; deal-specific risk | HIGH       | Reject                      | CA MAE cross-ref; no NEC condition; Sch. 3.7 cabined
3  | Survival limitation period    | §3.3; Ex. B  | Exhibit B; Playbook; CA      | Materially off-market          | CRITICAL   | Walk-away if shortened      | Short period deleted; Ex. B controlling
4  | Basket deductible→tipping     | §5.1(c)      | Playbook preference          | Debtor-favorable mechanic      | MODERATE   | Concede (controlling email) | Tipping basket accepted expressly
5  | NEC waiting/cure lag          | §2.2–2.3     | Bank form; UCC practice      | Off-market                     | HIGH       | Reject                      | Immediate NEC; no Debtor cure
6  | Bank lien subordination thin  | §2.2(b), §5.3| Bank form; Playbook          | Incomplete                     | HIGH       | Require full subordination  | Subordination + customary exceptions inserted
7  | Sch. 3.7 spillover            | §1.1, §3.1, §4.1 | Schedules control rule   | Improper export into ACA       | HIGH       | Block spillover             | Disclosure preserved; control unaffected
8  | Sch. 5.2 shift via indemnity  | §5.1         | Schedules control rule       | Silent economic shift          | HIGH       | Prevent shift               | Excluded Matters include Sch. 5.2
9  | Missing Loan Doc / conflict   | §4.3, §8.4   | Playbook; CA                 | Omission                       | MODERATE   | Insert                      | Inserted
10 | Account detail / notices      | Sch. I–II; Ex. A | Playbook; Bank form       | Operational gap                | MODERATE   | Complete                    | Structured schedules + form NEC
11 | Jury waiver / NY UCC control  | §8.1–8.2     | Playbook; Bank form          | Omission                       | LOW–MOD    | Insert                      | Inserted
12 | Termination residual duties   | §7.1         | Playbook                     | Omission                       | MODERATE   | Insert                      | Accrued indemnity/survival preserved

================================================================================
V. MISSING PROTECTIONS CHECKLIST (PLAYBOOK / BANK FORM)
================================================================================

[ ] Immediate NEC effectiveness — ADDED in redline
[ ] Entitlement Orders without Debtor consent — ADDED
[ ] Bank subordination of liens/setoff (customary exceptions only) — ADDED
[ ] No competing control agreement rep/covenant — ADDED
[ ] Complete Schedule I account fields — ADDED template
[ ] Secured Party statement/access rights — ADDED
[ ] Debtor further assurances — ADDED
[ ] ACA = Loan Document; CA conflict rule as between Debtor and Secured Party — ADDED
[ ] Bank reliance and limited liability — ADDED
[ ] Fee/returned item/overdraft parameters consistent with Bank form — ADDED (Exhibit C)
[ ] Form NEC exhibit — ADDED (Exhibit A)
[ ] Survival matrix conformity to Exhibit B — RESTORED
[ ] Full indemnity cap + fundamental breaches outside cap — RESTORED/ADDED
[ ] Jury waiver; NY law; UCC control reference — ADDED
[ ] Prompt notice of levy/freeze/regulatory developments affecting Accounts — ADDED

================================================================================
VI. RECOMMENDED NEGOTIATING PACKAGE
================================================================================

Package A (Firm recommendation — reflected in aca-redline.docx):
  1. Survival: non-negotiable Exhibit B (walk-away).
  2. Cap: restore full; Excluded Matters including Sch. 5.2 and control breaches.
  3. Basket: concede tipping basket.
  4. MAE: reject regulatory carve-outs; cabin Sch. 3.7.
  5. Control mechanics: Bank-form immediate NEC and subordination — require.
  6. Checklist insertions: require as clean-up.

Do not trade Item 1 for Items 2–6. Item 3 is already conceded capital; do not re-trade it for a still-reduced cap.

================================================================================
VII. CONCLUSION
================================================================================

The counterparty ACA paper is workable as a control instrument only after the redline in aca-redline.docx. The three headline deviations are fully addressed in accordance with schedules and the controlling partner instruction: cap restored, basket conceded as tipping, MAE regulatory carve-outs rejected, and survival shortening rejected on a walk-away basis. Schedule 3.7 and Schedule 5.2 intersections are neutralized. Missing Bank-form and playbook protections are inserted.

Upon counterparty acceptance of the redline (or an agreed issues list tracking the matrix above), the ACA should be cleared for execution concurrently with confirmation that Schedule I account details match Bank books and Credit Agreement collateral schedules.

Attachments / Companion Deliverable:
  • aca-redline.docx — full tracked-changes response markup

END OF MEMORANDUM
